recipes.name: Sour Cream Mushroom Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, for garnish

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a 9x13 inch baking dish, combine the cream of chicken soup, cream of mushroom soup, sour cream, wine/broth, onion, mushrooms, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Mix all together. Arrange chicken breasts on top of mixture. Bake uncovered in the preheated oven for 1 hour or until chicken is tender and juices run clear.

raw_recipe.headline: Sour Cream Mushroom Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Much like a chicken stroganoff, with mushrooms and wine in a sour cream sauce. A terrific combination that goes down easy.

review.reviewBody: Very tasty. I made it in the crockpot and let it simmer all day. The chicken was so tender.

Delicious ! Like another review mentioned- I browned the chicken first and sauteed mushrooms in wine and onions before mixing in the cream of chicken soup, spices and sour cream mix. Plus, I added lemon juice into the mix and sliced lemons on top of chicken breast while baking. Served over pasta. Yummy!

I sauteed my mushrooms with the wine and mixed it in with my soup mix, I also browned my chicken first and added a chicken/garlic mix that uplifted the taste. I also used boneless Chicken Thighs, and put some of the great sauce on top of the chicken before I baked.

I used 3 cloves chopped garlic instead of garlic powder, and I used 2 medium shallots instead of the onions. Also, I used 1 pound of chicken tenders and 1 pound of boneless skinless thighs. The aroma was delightful when cooking. I baked it uncovered for 1 and a half hours on 350 degrees. Jasmine rice was what I placed on the plate topped with the chicken and sour cream mushroom sauce. Broccoli as a side works well. All ingredients were organic, and GMO free. Deliciously aromatic dish enjoyed by all. Will repeat this one with with changes I made for sure!

Would be a great crock pot dish. Chicken was bland. Sauce was semi tasty. I suggest sauté mushrooms and onions and use fresh garlic in lieu of garlic powder. Remove garlic onions and mushrooms and set aside. Brown chicken in a dash of olive oil. After chicken is browned add the vegetables back in the pan.

Way too much sauce! Also, because you put the chicken on top, it ends up having no flavoring. If I make this again, I will saute the onions and mushroom; salt, pepper, and garlic powder the chicken and brown it before putting it in the sauce. More mushrooms, too!

This was tasty. I prepared it in a saucepan on the stove instead. I also didn't have enough sour cream, so i finished the measurement with cottage cheese. I also added a splash of Cardamon and Ground Savory. Then i served it with a side of Dill and Buttered Carrots. Yum!

This was a very tasty meal. I made this with everything it called for except I used the chicken broth instead of the wine and it was excellent! I also did this on the stove top instead of the oven and then served it over pasta. Yummy!

Yum! I’ve always been a fan of “cream of” recipes since my mom always made them growing up so this is right up my alley. So I almost made this as written but didn’t have wine so used chicken stock as others suggested. I’ll try wine next time or maybe add a pinch of boullion powder or poultry seasoning to the stock as it lacked a little flavor. The only change I’d make to the written recipe is to double the mushrooms! When I had the leftovers the next night I sautéed my leftover mushrooms and added them on top and it was even better. Can’t wait to try this in the crockpot. I’ll be making this over and over!

This was really good! I cooked a rice blend (white, brown, wild) and put it underneath the soup mixture. It took 2 1/4 hours to cook! I would definitely precook the chicken next time and still bake it for 1 hours. Very good flavor!

Very simple, but very tasty! I subbed frozen peas for the mushrooms (don't like mushrooms, and the peas were on hand.) I also added one small can of diced green chiles, which upped the heat and flavor. Whenever I bake chicken, I do so with the lid on the baking pan; I think it helps keep the chicken moist. Perfect for a stress-free dinner party.
Too runny. Sour cream separated (grainy bits). Made exactly as stated except without cup of mushrooms as I forgot to buy at store. Served on rice. Will not make again.
Good but will use less sour cream next time ...we had enough for a meal later this week or freeze for next week
Did not use salt to reduce sodium. Used reduced sodium canned soups. Used lite sour cream.
The worst! Watery, Sour cream separated into grainy bits: Chicken breasts cooked fine sitting on top of the watery, separated mess
It was more soupy than expected. It paired nicely with linguine pasta and served as like a chicken marsala.
I used one can of Cream of Celery soup instead of the other two soups. I cut the amounts of ingredients down as I was only using two pieces of chicken.
Love this recipe. I added red peppers and hot red pepper flakes, and some curry powder.
i loved this recepie and my kids loved it too. I added a bit of water to loosed up the thickness of the sauce and added some safron to the chicken. It came out really delicious
